bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Import competition from cheaper ASEAN paper and global overcapacity — The Board's Report states the Paper and Packaging Board market remained volatile with cheaper imports from ASEAN countries impacting sales realization and profitability. The MD&A lists low cost imports and global overcapacity as a threat to the Indian paper industry, and expects the industry to continue facing short term challenges from import pressures and a weak domestic pricing environment. Content sourced from the Board's Report in this bundle and the SWOT and material-issues tables of the same annual report routed into the profile bundle.
- Wood and pulpwood raw-material availability and competition for wood sourcing — The MD&A SWOT lists dependence on wood availability as a weakness and competition for wood sourcing as a threat. The Company states the demand for pulpwood has increased exponentially while availability of wood, the primary raw material, remains a significant challenge and a primary concern for industry sustainability, complicating procurement of sustainably managed wood. Sourced from the profile bundle of the same annual report.
- Climate change impact on agro-based inputs — Identified by the Company as a material risk in the BRSR material responsible business conduct issues table: changing rainfall patterns and temperature shifts are impacting the availability and quality of agro-residues like bagasse and hardwood, which are key inputs for pulp production, with potential for increased raw material costs or supply disruptions. Mitigation includes diversifying input sources and improving raw material storage. This BRSR table was routed into the profile bundle of the same annual report.
- Global pulp price volatility — Identified by the Company as a material risk in the BRSR material responsible business conduct issues table, with international pulp prices remaining volatile due to geopolitical tensions and supply chain factors. The bundle text is truncated mid-sentence at this row. Routed into the profile bundle of the same annual report.
- Structural demand erosion in writing and printing paper from digitalization — The MD&A SWOT lists rising digitalization as a threat, and Marketing Management notes that increasing adoption of digital communication and electronic media continues to moderate growth in the writing and printing paper segment globally. This matters because writing and printing paper contributed 67% of turnover in FY 2025-26.
- High capital intensity and elevated raw material, energy, logistics and financing costs — The MD&A SWOT lists high capital intensity, high raw material and energy costs, and high logistics and financing costs as weaknesses of the Indian paper industry. The outlook section additionally flags elevated raw material costs and GST-related disruptions as short-term industry challenges.
- Regulatory, environmental and tax exposure — The MD&A SWOT lists regulatory and environmental challenges as an industry threat. The Board's Report discloses that the Finance Act 2026 amended Section 206(3) of the Income Tax Act 2025, requiring domestic companies continuing under the old tax regime to pay Minimum Alternate Tax and treat it as final tax, with no accrual of MAT Credit Entitlement on or after 1st April 2026 and forgoing MAT Credit Entitlement available as on 31st March 2026.
- Product and customer concentration in paper and paperboard, with limited export diversification — BRSR Section A shows writing and printing paper at 67% and packaging board at 29% of turnover, with cement at only 1%, so earnings depend almost entirely on paper and board pricing. Exports contribute 12% of total turnover across 60 countries, limiting the cushion against domestic price weakness.
- Governance and board-composition compliance lapses — The Corporate Governance Report discloses non-compliance in FY 2025-26 with Regulation 17(1)(a) of SEBI LODR from delay in the appointment of Independent Directors leading to non-compliance with required board composition, and with Regulation 19(1)(c) as the composition of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee was not in accordance with prescribed requirements. Similar lapses were recorded in FY 2023-24. Sourced from the governance_entities bundle of the same annual report.

outlook.body:
- Sustainability: blending advanced automation with green practices, operating on a 'Waste to Wealth' concept where most waste generated is reused, recycled or repurposed, and pursuing a circular-economy model that narrows and closes energy and material loops
- Innovation: an R&D department focused on sustainable product development, operational excellence through cutting-edge technology, and circular-economy integration that turns industrial by-products into high-utility resources
- Management of human resources: a People First approach investing in employee development, well-being and capability enhancement through structured training and executive development programmes
- Financial re-engineering with efficient cost management: benchmarking operations against defined performance standards and continuously monitoring actual performance against established targets, with focus on operational efficiency and cost optimisation
- Customer centricity: continuous engagement with customers, dealers and institutional buyers, with focus on service levels, product consistency, supply reliability and customer support across all business segments
- Continuous and sustainable growth: expanding manufacturing capability in line with market demand, having grown from 90,000 TPA at inception in 1985 to a total installed capacity of 600,000 TPA
- Expanding the value added and specialty product portfolio and optimising product mix towards higher contribution grades
- Strengthening market presence across the paper, packaging board and tissue segments
- Increasing focus on import substitution and export opportunities
- Strengthening the dealer and distribution network by expanding into unrepresented markets, reinforcing existing channels and periodically evaluating dealer performance
- Shifting the board portfolio towards higher value added Virgin Fibre Board products including Folding Box Board, SBS Boards, Cup Stock and specialty packaging grades following the commissioning of the pulp mill at Unit II
- Developing export-oriented high bulk grades, specialty boards and higher GSM products to improve realisations and operational efficiencies
- Introducing sustainable packaging solutions such as Aqueous Barrier Coated products as environmentally friendly alternatives to conventional poly coated substrates
- Evaluating opportunities in the growing tissue paper segment in line with increasing hygiene awareness and demand from healthcare, hospitality and institutional sectors
- Digital transformation and Industry 4.0: Oracle EBS ERP-integrated eProcurement, AI and ML based production planning across paper machines, Advanced Process Control to optimise chemical consumption, a Decision Support System with an edge-computing Centralised Energy Management System, and Power BI dashboards with Python-based forecasting
- Backward integration into raw material through farm forestry and captive plantations to secure fibre supply
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: TNPL has grown by successive brownfield expansions, scaling Unit I at Kagithapuram from 90,000 tonnes per annum at inception in 1985 to 400,000 TPA today, and adding Unit II at Mondipatti, a 200,000 MT per annum packaging board plant completed in a record 22 months from the start of civil construction. Prior expansion milestones include a deinked pulp (DIP) line commissioned in 2013 - the first fine paper-grade DIP plant of its kind in India - and, as part of MEP Phase I at Unit II, a hardwood ECF pulpmill and chemical recovery island commissioned in July 2023. The current expansion programme has three live projects. First, a Tissue Paper Machine at Unit II: capitalising on the growing market potential for tissue paper, TNPL has established a modern 100 TPD tissue paper machine with associated advanced auxiliaries at a project cost of Rs 350 Crore, featuring a 6-metre Yankee dryer and designed to make grades from 13 GSM to 40 GSM using premium in-house hardwood pulp; the plant is presently undergoing advanced trial runs and operational stabilisation and is progressing towards full-scale commercial operations for domestic and export markets. Second, a Revamp of the Steam and Power System at Unit I: TNPL is modernising steam and power infrastructure in two phases, phasing out and replacing four low-pressure boilers commissioned at the mill's inception in 1985; the overall modernisation plan envisages two high-pressure boilers each with a steam generation capacity of 125 TPH at 105 ATA and 525 degrees C along with a 42 MW turbine generator, and Phase I - an Atmospheric Fluidised Bed Combustion (AFBC) boiler with a dedicated Fuel Handling Plant - is at an advanced stage of completion at a project cost of Rs 250 Crore. Third, rooftop solar: 1 MW rooftop solar power plants have been installed at each of the two manufacturing units, commissioned between June and August 2025. Alongside these, the Company operates an approximately 900 tonnes per day cement plant that converts lime sludge and fly ash into cement (a first in the Indian paper industry) with cement kiln flue gas used for on-site Precipitated Calcium Carbonate production, and the mill is actively evaluating a transition toward zero liquid discharge using next-generation treatment technologies. Land for the Multilayer Coated Board Plant at Mondipatti - 39.50 acres of Government Poramboke land granted under G.O. No. 447 dated 11.11.2013 - is still pending transfer of title and regular alienation in favour of the Company.

outlook.body:
- India continues to offer significant long term growth potential due to low per capita paper consumption compared to global averages
- Growth in education, organized retail, food delivery, healthcare, e-commerce and sustainable packaging sectors are expected to support future industry growth
- The Indian paper industry is expected to continue facing short term challenges arising from import pressures, elevated raw material costs, GST-related disruptions, weak domestic pricing environment and global economic uncertainties
- Demand conditions in certain paper and packaging grades may remain moderate in the near term, but long-term demand fundamentals for paper, packaging board and tissue products continue to remain positive, supported by India's economic growth, increasing organized consumption, sustainability trends and rising environmental awareness
- Increasing adoption of digital communication and electronic media continues to moderate growth in the writing and printing paper segment globally; however India's large student population and educational demand continue to support stable consumption in notebooks, publishing and educational grades
- Opportunity from growth in sustainable packaging solutions and rising preference for recyclable and biodegradable materials, including plastic replacement opportunities
- Increasing demand from FMCG, food service and e-commerce sectors
- Expansion in healthcare and hygiene-related tissue products
- Import substitution opportunities in premium grades and export opportunities in value added grades
- Availability of in-house pulp following commissioning of the Unit II pulp mill provides both input cost advantage and consistency in raw material quality
- Threats to the industry from low cost imports and global overcapacity, rising digitalization, regulatory and environmental challenges, and competition for wood sourcing
- The Paper and Packaging Board market remained volatile with cheaper imports from ASEAN countries impacting sales realization and profitability; the company is focusing on increasing market share of higher realization products and new premium products to improve profitability

currentContext.expansion: TNPL has grown by successive brownfield expansions, scaling Unit I at Kagithapuram from 90,000 tonnes per annum at inception in 1985 to 400,000 TPA today, and adding Unit II at Mondipatti, a 200,000 MT per annum packaging board plant completed in a record 22 months from the start of civil construction. Prior expansion milestones include a deinked pulp (DIP) line commissioned in 2013 - the first fine paper-grade DIP plant of its kind in India - and, as part of MEP Phase I at Unit II, a hardwood ECF pulpmill and chemical recovery island commissioned in July 2023. The current expansion programme has three live projects. First, a Tissue Paper Machine at Unit II: capitalising on the growing market potential for tissue paper, TNPL has established a modern 100 TPD tissue paper machine with associated advanced auxiliaries at a project cost of Rs 350 Crore, featuring a 6-metre Yankee dryer and designed to make grades from 13 GSM to 40 GSM using premium in-house hardwood pulp; the plant is presently undergoing advanced trial runs and operational stabilisation and is progressing towards full-scale commercial operations for domestic and export markets. Second, a Revamp of the Steam and Power System at Unit I: TNPL is modernising steam and power infrastructure in two phases, phasing out and replacing four low-pressure boilers commissioned at the mill's inception in 1985; the overall modernisation plan envisages two high-pressure boilers each with a steam generation capacity of 125 TPH at 105 ATA and 525 degrees C along with a 42 MW turbine generator, and Phase I - an Atmospheric Fluidised Bed Combustion (AFBC) boiler with a dedicated Fuel Handling Plant - is at an advanced stage of completion at a project cost of Rs 250 Crore. Third, rooftop solar: 1 MW rooftop solar power plants have been installed at each of the two manufacturing units, commissioned between June and August 2025. Alongside these, the Company operates an approximately 900 tonnes per day cement plant that converts lime sludge and fly ash into cement (a first in the Indian paper industry) with cement kiln flue gas used for on-site Precipitated Calcium Carbonate production, and the mill is actively evaluating a transition toward zero liquid discharge using next-generation treatment technologies. Land for the Multilayer Coated Board Plant at Mondipatti - 39.50 acres of Government Poramboke land granted under G.O. No. 447 dated 11.11.2013 - is still pending transfer of title and regular alienation in favour of the Company.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Tamil Nadu Newsprint and Papers Limited (TNPL) is one of Asia's largest bagasse-based paper producers, promoted by the Government of Tamil Nadu, with an aggregate paper and paperboard capacity of 6,00,000 TPA across two units in Tamil Nadu.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: TNPL manufactures printing and writing paper, multilayer coated packaging board and cement across Unit I at Kagithapuram (Karur District) and Unit II at Mondipatti (Tiruchirappalli District), Tamil Nadu. It pioneered the use of bagasse, a sugarcane residue, as its primary fibre, complemented by hardwood pulp from captive and farm-forestry plantations and recycled fibre from its deinking plant. Customers span dealers, government agencies, public sector undertakings, educational institutions and direct consumers across publishing, education, food processing, textiles, pharmaceuticals and manufacturing, with cement sold to construction contractors, real estate developers and building material traders.

demand_drivers.body:
- India continues to offer significant long term growth potential due to low per capita paper consumption compared to global averages
- Growth in education, organized retail, food delivery, healthcare, e-commerce and sustainable packaging sectors are expected to support future industry growth
- The Indian paper industry is expected to continue facing short term challenges arising from import pressures, elevated raw material costs, GST-related disruptions, weak domestic pricing environment and global economic uncertainties
- Demand conditions in certain paper and packaging grades may remain moderate in the near term, but long-term demand fundamentals for paper, packaging board and tissue products continue to remain positive, supported by India's economic growth, increasing organized consumption, sustainability trends and rising environmental awareness
- Increasing adoption of digital communication and electronic media continues to moderate growth in the writing and printing paper segment globally; however India's large student population and educational demand continue to support stable consumption in notebooks, publishing and educational grades
- Opportunity from growth in sustainable packaging solutions and rising preference for recyclable and biodegradable materials, including plastic replacement opportunities
- Increasing demand from FMCG, food service and e-commerce sectors
- Expansion in healthcare and hygiene-related tissue products
- Import substitution opportunities in premium grades and export opportunities in value added grades
- Availability of in-house pulp following commissioning of the Unit II pulp mill provides both input cost advantage and consistency in raw material quality
- Threats to the industry from low cost imports and global overcapacity, rising digitalization, regulatory and environmental challenges, and competition for wood sourcing
- The Paper and Packaging Board market remained volatile with cheaper imports from ASEAN countries impacting sales realization and profitability; the company is focusing on increasing market share of higher realization products and new premium products to improve profitability

margins.body: Margins pressured by 30-40% wood cost inflation (domestic supply shortage post-COVID planting dip), import competition from China/Indonesia, and higher freight costs for imported inputs; HWP and bagasse pulp integration partially offsets raw material volatility.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing capex for growth (tissue, power, solar); maintaining dividend payout (interim Rs. 3 + final Rs. 1/share = Rs. 4/share total); reducing net debt by Rs. 65cr; no bonus issue planned currently; reserve surplus of Rs. 2,020cr held for future strategic moves.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: TNPL has grown by successive brownfield expansions, scaling Unit I at Kagithapuram from 90,000 tonnes per annum at inception in 1985 to 400,000 TPA today, and adding Unit II at Mondipatti, a 200,000 MT per annum packaging board plant completed in a record 22 months from the start of civil construction. Prior expansion milestones include a deinked pulp (DIP) line commissioned in 2013 - the first fine paper-grade DIP plant of its kind in India - and, as part of MEP Phase I at Unit II, a hardwood ECF pulpmill and chemical recovery island commissioned in July 2023. The current expansion programme has three live projects. First, a Tissue Paper Machine at Unit II: capitalising on the growing market potential for tissue paper, TNPL has established a modern 100 TPD tissue paper machine with associated advanced auxiliaries at a project cost of Rs 350 Crore, featuring a 6-metre Yankee dryer and designed to make grades from 13 GSM to 40 GSM using premium in-house hardwood pulp; the plant is presently undergoing advanced trial runs and operational stabilisation and is progressing towards full-scale commercial operations for domestic and export markets. Second, a Revamp of the Steam and Power System at Unit I: TNPL is modernising steam and power infrastructure in two phases, phasing out and replacing four low-pressure boilers commissioned at the mill's inception in 1985; the overall modernisation plan envisages two high-pressure boilers each with a steam generation capacity of 125 TPH at 105 ATA and 525 degrees C along with a 42 MW turbine generator, and Phase I - an Atmospheric Fluidised Bed Combustion (AFBC) boiler with a dedicated Fuel Handling Plant - is at an advanced stage of completion at a project cost of Rs 250 Crore. Third, rooftop solar: 1 MW rooftop solar power plants have been installed at each of the two manufacturing units, commissioned between June and August 2025. Alongside these, the Company operates an approximately 900 tonnes per day cement plant that converts lime sludge and fly ash into cement (a first in the Indian paper industry) with cement kiln flue gas used for on-site Precipitated Calcium Carbonate production, and the mill is actively evaluating a transition toward zero liquid discharge using next-generation treatment technologies. Land for the Multilayer Coated Board Plant at Mondipatti - 39.50 acres of Government Poramboke land granted under G.O. No. 447 dated 11.11.2013 - is still pending transfer of title and regular alienation in favour of the Company.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledges headwinds but emphasizes long-term sustainability, import substitution opportunity, and product innovation; confident in capex execution; avoids overpromising on growth or margin recovery; tone is pragmatic, state-owned enterprise discipline evident.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Fibre security through a backward-integrated agro-forestry ecosystem: captive and farm-forestry plantations cumulatively spanning over 3.09 lakh acres involving more than 66,273 farmers, supported by company-supplied high-yielding clonal plants and a buy-back guarantee
- Raw-material cost and sustainability advantage from pioneering bagasse, a renewable by-product of the sugar industry, as the primary fibre, significantly reducing dependency on forest-based resources
- Integrated, resource-efficient manufacturing with in-house chemical bagasse and deinked pulping, and in-house hardwood pulp at Unit II giving both input cost advantage and consistency in raw material quality
- Energy self-sufficiency: captive power generation of 153.62 MW plus 35.5 MW of wind farm; TNPL is 100% self-sufficient in power and exports surplus
- Circular-economy waste monetisation: the first mill in the Indian paper industry to manufacture superior grade cement from lime sludge and fly ash, with cement kiln flue gas used for on-site production of Precipitated Calcium Carbonate
- Among the lowest specific water consumption rates in the Indian paper industry through advanced process optimisation and effluent recycling
- FSC dual certification, which the Company states provides a platform to strengthen the export market where certified products play a vital role in marketing
- Established brand portfolio and dealer distribution network, with brands including TNPL Ace Marvel, Radiant Platinum, Printer's Choice and TNPL Copier, being expanded into unrepresented markets
- Government of Tamil Nadu promoter backing, holding 35.32% of the equity

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Persistent import competition from low-cost Asian paper; wood price volatility; subdued domestic demand due to digital substitution; global shipping disruptions increasing input costs; capex execution delays; regulatory pressure on single-use plastics creating mixed signals.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: TNPL’s bio-methanation plant generates 83.06 lakh NM methane gas — replacing 4,464 KL furnace oil and 707 MT coal — creating hidden cost savings and ESG premium not reflected in P&L; wind farm (35.5 MW) generates 372.82 lakh kWh green power — effectively subsidizing energy costs; 22,982-acre clonal plantation program locks in future pulp supply and creates rural stakeholder alignment.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Sustainability: blending advanced automation with green practices, operating on a 'Waste to Wealth' concept where most waste generated is reused, recycled or repurposed, and pursuing a circular-economy model that narrows and closes energy and material loops
- Innovation: an R&D department focused on sustainable product development, operational excellence through cutting-edge technology, and circular-economy integration that turns industrial by-products into high-utility resources
- Management of human resources: a People First approach investing in employee development, well-being and capability …
